intro: To change slide size in PowerPoint on Mac, open File > Page Setup. Pick a preset from the Slide sized for list, or choose Custom and type your own width and height.
tldr: Open File > Page Setup in PowerPoint for Mac.
Pick a preset in Slide sized for, or choose Custom and enter a width and height.
Custom sizes must fall between 1 and 56 inches on each side.
If PowerPoint asks Scale or Don't Scale, choose Scale when your content should resize with the slide.
Check every slide afterward, because the size applies to the whole deck.

blocks.text: Slide size is a file-wide setting. You change it once, and every slide follows. That is why it helps to settle the size before you build layouts, charts and speaker notes. A change late in a project can move text and pictures out of place.
Where the setting lives in PowerPoint for Mac

The main route is File > Page Setup. Microsoft's Mac article documents it for Microsoft 365 for Mac, PowerPoint 2024 for Mac and PowerPoint 2021 for Mac. Microsoft's general article gives a second route: the Design tab, then Slide Size, then Page Setup for custom sizes. Both lead to the same settings. Use whichever path your menu shows.
The Design route also lists Standard (4:3) and Widescreen (16:9) directly. That is quicker for the two common shapes. Custom sizes still need the Page Setup dialog.
Pick a preset or enter a custom size
Presets are the fastest route. Use one when your deck needs a standard shape, such as Widescreen (16:9). Choose Custom when a venue, a printer or a template asks for something else.

items: Preset: pick it from the Slide sized for list, or use Standard (4:3) and Widescreen (16:9) on the Design tab.
Custom: choose Custom, then type a width and height in the boxes.
Units: inches, centimeters and pixels are all accepted in the dialog.
Limits: inches must fall between 1 and 56 on each side.

blocks.text: Custom slide size in PowerPoint on Mac: limits and units

Custom dimensions have hard limits. Microsoft says each side must fall between 1 and 56 inches. In centimeters, that range is 2.54 to 142.24 cm. In pixels, it is 120 to 720 px. Enter a number inside the range, or PowerPoint will not accept it.

A common surprise is a request for an oversize slide. A print vendor or a large venue might ask for a very wide format. If the request goes past 56 inches, Page Setup cannot hold it. Split the content across slides, or ask the vendor for a format within the limit.
Scale or Don't Scale when you change slide size

After a size change, PowerPoint may ask how to handle content. The choice is Scale or Don't Scale. Scale resizes text, pictures and shapes to match the new slide. Don't Scale keeps each object at its current size, so it can run past the edges.

Some third-party write-ups describe Maximize or Ensure Fit in newer builds. Microsoft has not confirmed those labels in the pages we checked. Trust the prompt on your screen, and read it before you click.

blocks.text: Pick the choice, then check the deck. If the layout breaks, undo with ⌘ Z and try the other option. Undo is faster than repairing every slide by hand.
Orientation affects notes and handouts too

The Orientation setting controls which way your slides run. Microsoft says the same setting also applies to notes and handouts. Print a test page of each before you hand out a deck. A slide that fits well can still leave a notes page looking off.
Why every slide must share one size

PowerPoint keeps one slide size for the whole presentation. You cannot resize a single slide on its own. A size change applies only to the current presentation, unless you save the size as a custom default theme.
If one slide truly needs another shape, put it in a separate file. Export that slide as an image or a PDF, then place it in the main deck. The main deck keeps its size.
Set a custom size as the default for new decks

If your team builds every deck at one size, save that size as a theme. Microsoft's steps start in Page Setup. Then you save the theme and mark it as the default. New presentations pick up the size from then on.

items: Set the width, height and Orientation in File > Page Setup, then click OK.
On the Design tab, click the More arrow beside the themes.
Under Custom, right-click the theme, then choose Set as Default Theme.

blocks.text: Test the default with a new blank deck before you rely on it. Existing files keep their own size, so they will not change on their own.
Worked example: moving a 4:3 deck to widescreen

Here is a common case. You have an older 4:3 deck, and the conference room needs 16:9. Open the Design tab, click Slide Size, then choose Widescreen (16:9). PowerPoint then asks how to handle the content.

For a text-heavy deck, Scale usually keeps content on the slide, because it resizes objects with the new frame. Then go slide by slide. Check charts against their labels, and check footers near the bottom edge.
Work in order. Fix one slide, then move to the next. Keep the original file open as a reference, so you can compare the two versions side by side.
Common mistakes with slide size on Mac

items: Changing the size after the layouts are final, then fixing each slide by hand.
Choosing Don't Scale without checking the edges of every slide.
Typing a value above 56 inches or below 1 inch, then wondering why it fails.
Expecting one slide to differ from the rest. Every slide shares one size.
Changing Orientation and forgetting that notes and handouts follow it.

blocks.text: When the menus look different on your Mac

Microsoft's two articles name the path slightly differently. The Mac article says File > Page Setup. The general article says Design > Slide Size > Page Setup. Your build may show either one, or both. Look under File first, then under Design.

Build numbers help when a menu does not match. The newest build in Microsoft's release notes when we checked is 16.114.3, dated October 27, 2026. Those notes list quality and performance fixes. They do not mention slide size, Page Setup or the Design tab.
Is there a keyboard shortcut or a faster Mac option?

No Mac keyboard shortcut for slide size appears in the Microsoft pages we checked. The menu route is the documented route. Some people set a custom default theme once, then skip the dialog for every new deck.

A third-party report describes a Mac slide-size pane with live resizing and social media presets. The report gave an October 2026 preview target and a November 2026 release target. In our check, that pane was not released. The report is secondary, so treat the date as a plan.
PowerPoint for the web uses a different path

PowerPoint for the web puts slide size under Design > Slide Size > Custom Slide Size. It takes inches only, within 1 to 56 inches. If you move between the web app and the Mac app, expect different units. Convert the numbers before you type them.
What to do after you change the size

Check the deck, then move to the tasks that depend on the layout. Speaker notes and narration are easier to set up once the size is final. Read the guides on [adding speaker notes in PowerPoint on Mac](/how-to/add-speaker-notes-in-powerpoint) and [recording a slide show in PowerPoint on Mac](/how-to/record-a-slide-show-in-powerpoint).

faq.question: Can I change the slide size for one slide only?
faq.answer: No. PowerPoint keeps one size for every slide in a presentation. To use a different shape for one slide, put that slide in a separate file, export it as an image or PDF, then place it in the main deck.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut for slide size on Mac?
faq.answer: Not in the Microsoft pages checked for this guide. Use the menu route instead: File > Page Setup, or Design > Slide Size. Check Microsoft's support pages for changes.

faq.question: What is the largest slide size I can set?
faq.answer: For custom sizes, each side can be up to 56 inches. That equals 142.24 cm, or 720 px at the pixel limit. The smallest allowed side is 1 inch, or 2.54 cm, or 120 px.

faq.question: What is the difference between Scale and Don't Scale?
faq.answer: Scale resizes text, pictures and shapes to fit the new slide. Don't Scale keeps objects at their current size, so they may run past the edges. Check every slide after you choose either one.

faq.question: Does changing the slide size affect my notes and handouts?
faq.answer: Yes, in one way. Microsoft says the Orientation setting also applies to notes and handouts. Check those pages after the change, since they follow the same orientation.

faq.question: Can I make my custom size the default for new decks?
faq.answer: Yes. Set the size in File > Page Setup, then choose Save Current Theme from the More arrow beside the themes. Right-click the saved theme under Custom and choose Set as Default Theme.

faq.question: Why does my Mac show different menu names?
faq.answer: Microsoft names the path in two ways, and builds can differ. Open the PowerPoint menu and choose About PowerPoint to find your build. Compare that build with Microsoft's release notes.

faq.question: Is a slide-size pane coming to PowerPoint for Mac?
faq.answer: A third-party report says Microsoft planned a Mac slide-size pane with live resizing for November 2026. It was not listed as released in the pages we checked. Treat that as a plan until Microsoft confirms it.

steps.name: Open the presentation
steps.text: Open the deck in PowerPoint for Mac. Slide size applies to the whole file, so you do not need to select a slide first. Save a copy before you start.
steps.tip: A copy lets you compare the old and new sizes side by side.

steps.name: Open the File menu
steps.text: Click File in the menu bar at the top of the screen, while the deck window is active.

steps.name: Choose Page Setup
steps.text: Click Page Setup. The Page Setup dialog opens with the size and orientation settings.
steps.tip: If you do not see Page Setup under File, read the troubleshooting section below.

steps.name: Open the Slide sized for list
steps.text: In the Size section, click the Slide sized for list. It shows the preset sizes that PowerPoint offers.

steps.name: Pick a preset or choose Custom
steps.text: Click a preset to use it. To set your own size, click Custom.

steps.name: Enter a width and height
steps.text: For a custom size, type the width and height in the boxes. You can use inches, centimeters or pixels. Each side must fall within the limits: 1 to 56 inches.
steps.tip: Stay inside the limits, or PowerPoint will not accept the value.

steps.name: Set the Orientation
steps.text: Choose the Orientation that matches your slides. The setting also applies to notes and handouts, so check those after you save.

steps.name: Click OK and answer the prompt
steps.text: Click OK. If PowerPoint asks Scale or Don't Scale, read the choice before you click. Scale resizes content to fit. Don't Scale keeps objects at their current size.
steps.tip: When in doubt, choose Scale, then check each slide.

steps.name: Check every slide
steps.text: Scroll through the whole deck. Look at text near the edges, charts, pictures and footers. Fix any slide that now looks crowded or cut off.

steps.name: Save the file
steps.text: Press ⌘ S to save. Save under a new name if you want to keep the old size as a backup.

troubleshooting.problem: Page Setup does not appear under File
troubleshooting.fix: Make sure a presentation is open and active, then check the File menu again. If it is still missing, try Design > Slide Size, which Microsoft's general article says leads to Page Setup for custom sizes.

troubleshooting.problem: Content runs off the edges after the change
troubleshooting.fix: Undo with ⌘ Z, then change the size again and choose Scale. If the layout still breaks, adjust the slide master layouts so new content fits the new frame.

troubleshooting.problem: PowerPoint will not accept my width or height
troubleshooting.fix: Check the range. Inches must fall between 1 and 56. Centimeters must fall between 2.54 and 142.24. Pixels must fall between 120 and 720.

troubleshooting.problem: The prompt says Maximize or Ensure Fit, not Scale
troubleshooting.fix: Read the options on your screen and choose the one that keeps your content in view. Microsoft's pages describe Scale or Don't Scale. Third-party reports mention newer labels that Microsoft has not confirmed.

troubleshooting.problem: One slide needs a different shape from the rest
troubleshooting.fix: All slides share one size. Move that slide to a separate file, export it as an image or PDF, then place it in the main deck.

troubleshooting.problem: Notes or handouts look wrong after the change
troubleshooting.fix: Orientation applies to notes and handouts too. Reopen Page Setup and confirm the Orientation, then check the notes pages in Print Preview.
